The rating is too low relative to the growth the desk itself feeds in.

Reality Labs lost $19.2bn on $2.2bn revenue (PERF-7, PERF-9) while Family of Apps earned $102.5bn (PERF-8). The model treats the consolidated 38% margin as durable; if RL losses are a permanent drag, the base case is too high — but if RL is optionality the market is not paying for, the rating is too low. Either way the segment split is ignored.

terminal_share is 0.781 and terminal_excess_return is set to 1.0 (full moat), with terminal_roic held at today's 23.87% versus an 8.87% WACC. Nearly four-fifths of value rests on a perpetuity assuming Meta's excess return never fades, despite RISK-1 through RISK-6 (regulation, AI competition, copyright litigation). A 0.5 moat share would cut the base materially and push price/fair-value toward Underweight.

sbc_to_revenue is 11.01% and is expensed, but cash_conversion of 1.927 (OCF/NOPAT) is far above 1, meaning NOPAT understates cash generation — the model's own caution threshold is 0.8. A 1.93 conversion with 11% SBC and $72bn capex (CAP-7) suggests the reinvestment charge via sales_to_capital (0.891) is too light, flattering the base fair value and the Overweight.

why: price / base fair value 1.32 at High uncertainty (volatility 23%, range 1.72x base): Buy at or below 0.60, Overweight to 0.90, Underweight from 1.11, Sell from 1.55

objections.argument: The desk's growth_used of -0.21% comes from a 10-K figure that is distorted by two COVID products. PERF-3 shows revenue rose 6% operationally ex-Comirnaty/Paxlovid, and PERF-7 shows Biopharma earnings of $29.3bn on $61.2bn revenue (~48% margin) versus the 21.7% operating_margin used. The base case is built on a declining, low-margin business that the evidence does not describe.

The DCF charges the full Metsera acquisition ($8.0bn consideration, CAP-7; $6.9bn cash, CAP-8) as reinvestment while capital_for_reinvestment excludes acquired intangibles from the sales-to-capital denominator. Growth bought with M&A is therefore penalised twice: cash out, no revenue credit. That mechanically depresses fair_value and inflates price/base.

terminal_growth is set to the risk-free rate (4.75%) while implied_growth is 3.76% and growth_used is -0.21%. A terminal growth above the near-term growth path, plus terminal_share of 53.5%, means most of the value sits in a perpetuity growing faster than the explicit forecast — an internally inconsistent, value-inflating construction that argues the rating is too low, not too high.

The rating ignores capital returns and balance-sheet capacity. CAP-3 shows $3.3bn of buyback authorisation unused, CAP-4 a $0.43 quarterly dividend, and CAP-1 $12.5bn short-term investments against CAP-2 $62bn long-term debt. A 1.32x price/base with a 23% volatility and a 1.72x range is not a high-conviction Underweight given this cash generation (PERF-5: $11.7bn OCF).

A 21.7% operating margin on a business with that earnings base may understate normalized profitability, arguing the rating is too low.

A zero tax rate inflates NOPAT and fair value, so the Underweight may be too harsh.
